_note: Shared content for all five storefront demos. Identical everywhere, so the only variable a customer is judging is the DESIGN.

practitioner.name: Aurelia Sable
practitioner.tagline: Tarot for people at a crossroads
practitioner.short_bio: I read for people who already know something has to change and want a clearer look at it. Seventeen years, mostly by referral.
practitioner.long_bio:
I started reading for friends in a flat in Bangalore with a borrowed deck and no idea what I was doing. Seventeen years later I read full time, mostly for people sent by someone I have already read for.

I do not predict. A reading is a structured hour of attention on a question you have been circling alone, and the cards are the structure. Most people arrive knowing the answer and needing to hear it said out loud by someone with no stake in it.

I will not read on someone else's behalf, I will not tell you whether to leave a marriage, and I will not pretend a spread can replace a doctor, a lawyer or a therapist. Everything else is fair game.

services.name: The Threshold Reading
services.blurb: One question, held properly. For a decision you have been carrying too long.
services.detail: A focused spread on a single crossroads. You bring one real question — not five — and we spend the whole session on it. Best for a decision with a deadline attached.

services.name: The Full Life Reading
services.blurb: The long look. Work, love, family, money — and how they are pulling against each other.
services.detail: A wide spread across every area at once, which is the only way to see where one part of your life is quietly paying for another. People usually book this at the start of a year or the end of something.
includes: A second session at half price within 90 days

services.name: The Year Ahead
services.blurb: Twelve cards, twelve months, and the two that actually matter.
services.detail: A month-by-month spread read as a shape rather than a forecast — where the pressure gathers, where it lifts, and which two months are worth clearing your calendar for.

services.name: The Written Reading
services.blurb: No camera, no calendar. Send the question, receive the reading.
services.detail: For people in awkward time zones, or who simply think better on paper. You send your question in writing; I read and send back roughly 1,200 words, plus photographs of the spread.

services.name: The Voice Note
services.blurb: Fifteen minutes, spoken. The smallest way in.
services.detail: A short spoken reading on one narrow question. Most people book this first to see whether we get on before spending more.

faq.q: Do I need to have a question ready?
faq.a: It helps, but no. Plenty of people arrive with a mess rather than a question, and shaping it is part of the session.
No. I read what is already in motion and where it is likely to lead if nothing changes. That is a different thing, and more useful.

faq.q: What if I do not like what comes up?
faq.a: Then we sit with it. I will not soften a reading to keep the session comfortable, and I will not dramatise one to make it memorable.

faq.q: Can you read about someone who is not present?
faq.a: Only as far as they affect you. I will not read another person's private life on your behalf.
It is not, and it does not replace it. If something surfaces that needs a professional, I will say so plainly.
You get a confirmation with a calendar invite and a link. Ten minutes before, you get a reminder. That is the whole process.

booking_steps.detail: Five formats, from a fifteen-minute voice note to a ninety-minute session.
Live availability in your own time zone. No back-and-forth by message.
Card or UPI. You are charged once, at the time of booking.
A calendar invite for live sessions; an email for written and audio ones.

policies.cancellation: Free up to 24 hours before. Inside 24 hours, the session is held as credit for 90 days.
policies.disclaimer: Readings are offered for reflection and entertainment. They are not medical, legal, financial or psychological advice.
